# Dynadot Provider

Manage registered nameservers using Dynadot REST v1. Terraform 1.14+ is required for actions. External nameservers, domain delegation, DNS records, and Registry publication are deferred.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "dynadot" {
  # Set DYNADOT_API_KEY in the environment.
  sandbox = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) Dynadot API key. Defaults to DYNADOT_API_KEY when omitted.
- `sandbox` (Boolean) Use the Dynadot sandbox API. Defaults to false.

## Automatic limits

Configuration discovers `data.account_info.price_level` through `GET /accounts/info`, initially at Regular limits. Every new configuration rediscovers the tier; account responses are not stored in state or logged.

| Account tier | Requests/second | Requests/minute | Maximum concurrent requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Regular | 1 | 60 | 1 |
| Bulk | 10 | 600 | 5 |
| Super Bulk | 100 | 6,000 | 35 |

Tier matching ignores case, whitespace, hyphens, and underscores. Unknown or missing tiers warn and use Regular limits; discovery failures fail configuration after bounded retries. Requests and retries share no-burst pacing and a separate concurrency ceiling across resources and actions. HTTP/API 429 responses set a shared `Retry-After` cooldown, defaulting to 60 seconds. All waits respect cancellation and operation deadlines.

Separate provider processes and other API consumers share your account quota. Local throttling cannot coordinate them. See [Dynadot's API documentation](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/api-document) for API settings and limits; select v1.
